reason: Both replies rightly drop "proven hit" and work through the budget. A's questions match what the user actually knows: whether the game is finished, a delivery date and what happens if it slips (the refund promise), who gave the 23 ratings (mostly people at the user's convention table), and whether any reviews are lined up (the 90k-subscriber YouTuber). Those answers are what will reassure a wary backer who has lost money before, and B's broader cost checklist misses the reviewer and where the ratings came from.
